de:
Das Modell kann die von der Kanzlei ausgewählten Dokumente und Mitteilungen, noch nicht veröffentlichte Logos und Fotos, Namen und Biografien von Personen, Kontaktdaten, Leistungen, Qualifikationen, bestätigte Fakten und Rechtstexte erhalten. Zur Erstellung des Briefings kann es jede ausgewählte Quelle vollständig lesen. Für jede Quelle hält das Briefing den beruflichen Zweck, den weiteren Bedarf und die genaue Seite, Passage oder Datei fest. Der Code prüft nur, ob jede Quelle abgedeckt ist und der Plan die erforderliche Struktur hat; er entscheidet nicht über die fachliche Relevanz.

Erstellung und Prüfung verwenden danach das Briefing, nur diese Materialien, Struktur- und Textentwürfe, Website-Dateien sowie Desktop- und Telefon-Screenshots. Eine vollständige Quelle wird nur erneut geöffnet, wenn der Plan sie aus einem dokumentierten beruflichen Grund als notwendig ausweist. Es greift nicht auf das allgemeine Kanzleiarchiv, Mandantenakten, das Postfach oder nicht ausgewählte Dateien zu.

Das Modell erhält Quellen innerhalb derselben Grenzen; der optionale OpenAI-Sites-Adapter und Veröffentlichungsweg ist nur in Codex verfügbar. Es erfolgt keine automatische Anonymisierung.
en:
The model may receive the documents and communications selected by the firm, unpublished logos and photographs, people's names and biographies, contact details, services, qualifications, confirmed facts, and legal text. To prepare the brief, the model may read each selected source in full. For every source, the brief records its professional purpose, whether it is still needed, and the exact page, excerpt, or asset required. Code checks only that every source is covered and that the plan has the required shape; it does not decide what is professionally relevant.

Building and review then use the brief, only those materials, proposed structure and copy, site files, and desktop and phone screenshots. A full source is reopened only when the plan marks it as necessary for a recorded professional reason. It does not access the firm's general archive, client matters, mailbox, or unselected files.

The model receives sources within the same limits; the optional OpenAI Sites adapter and publication route is available only in Codex. There is no automatic anonymization.
es:
El modelo puede recibir los documentos y comunicaciones elegidos por el despacho, logotipos y fotografías aún no publicados, nombres y biografías de personas, datos de contacto, servicios, cualificaciones, hechos confirmados y textos legales. Para preparar el brief, puede leer íntegramente cada fuente seleccionada. Para cada fuente, el brief registra su finalidad profesional, si sigue siendo necesaria y la página, el extracto o el recurso exacto requerido. El código solo comprueba que cada fuente esté cubierta y que el plan tenga la estructura requerida; no decide la relevancia profesional.

La construcción y la revisión usan después el brief, únicamente esos materiales, la estructura y los borradores de texto, los archivos del sitio y las capturas de ordenador y teléfono. Una fuente completa se vuelve a abrir solo cuando el plan la considera necesaria por una razón profesional registrada. No accede al archivo general del despacho, a expedientes de clientes, al correo ni a archivos no seleccionados.

El modelo recibe las fuentes dentro de los mismos límites; la ruta opcional de adaptación y publicación de OpenAI Sites solo está disponible en Codex. No hay anonimización automática.
fr:
Le modèle peut recevoir les documents et communications choisis par le cabinet, les logos et photographies non encore publiés, les noms et biographies des personnes, les coordonnées, les services, les qualifications, les faits confirmés et les textes juridiques. Pour préparer le brief, il peut lire intégralement chaque source sélectionnée. Pour chaque source, le brief consigne sa finalité professionnelle, si elle reste nécessaire et la page, l'extrait ou la ressource exacte requise. Le code vérifie seulement que chaque source est couverte et que le plan respecte la structure requise ; il ne décide pas de la pertinence professionnelle.

La construction et la revue utilisent ensuite le brief, ces seuls éléments, la structure et les projets de textes, les fichiers du site et les captures sur ordinateur et téléphone. Une source complète n'est rouverte que si le plan la juge nécessaire pour une raison professionnelle consignée. Il n'accède pas aux archives générales du cabinet, aux dossiers clients, à la messagerie ni aux fichiers non sélectionnés.

Le modèle reçoit les sources dans les mêmes limites ; le parcours optionnel d'adaptation et de publication OpenAI Sites n'est disponible que dans Codex. Aucune anonymisation automatique n'est prévue.
it:
Possono entrare nel modello i documenti e le comunicazioni scelti dallo Studio, logo e fotografie non ancora pubblicati, nomi e biografie delle persone, recapiti, servizi, qualifiche, fatti confermati e testi legali. Per preparare il brief, il modello può leggere per intero ogni fonte selezionata. Per ciascuna fonte, il brief registra lo scopo professionale, se serve ancora e la pagina, l'estratto o la risorsa esatta necessaria. Il codice controlla soltanto che ogni fonte sia coperta e che il piano abbia la struttura richiesta; non decide che cosa sia professionalmente rilevante.

Costruzione e revisione usano poi il brief, quei soli materiali, struttura e bozze, file del sito e schermate desktop e telefono. Una fonte completa viene riaperta solo quando il piano la indica come necessaria per una ragione professionale registrata. Non accede all'archivio generale dello Studio, alle pratiche dei clienti, alla posta o a file non selezionati.

Il modello riceve le fonti entro gli stessi limiti; il percorso opzionale OpenAI Sites per adattare e pubblicare il sito è disponibile solo in Codex. Non è prevista anonimizzazione automatica.

security_controls.control: Workspace initialization requires asserted owner, retention owner, explicit user confirmation and an exact directory outside a Git repository or published static/shared root. Files, symlinks, filesystem roots, the home directory and non-empty unmanaged directories are rejected. Run outputs use owner-only permissions, atomic JSON replacement and a private staging directory before the run becomes visible.

Run preparation requires at least one regular non-symlink selected file or one exact fact explicitly confirmed by the user in conversation, and every selected item must carry approved_for_website_use=true for the website purpose. Files are copied into the private run and confirmed facts are serialized into immutable evidence snapshots; each records the website-use approval, byte size and SHA-256, duplicate evidence IDs are rejected and intake plus source register are bound to one digest. Every later gate rechecks the approval and rehashes the snapshots. A public URL alone is not treated as captured evidence.

The site brief records exactly one source-use item for every registered evidence ID. The model states the professional purpose and chooses mapped_brief_only, targeted_material or full_source_required; deterministic code verifies only schema shape, unique IDs and exact source-register coverage. Downstream design, copy and build work use mapped brief facts by default, reopen only the named targeted material when required, and use a complete selected source only when the recorded professional reason requires it. No deterministic keyword or personal-data classifier substitutes for that semantic judgment.

Information architecture, copy, visual direction and rendered quality remain model-led proposals. Every studio-profile field is labelled observed, user supplied or Vera default; observed and user-supplied fields require selected evidence IDs, and claim records cannot reference an unknown source ID. Deterministic code does not decide aesthetics, professional truth, accessibility compliance or legal sufficiency.

The validator recomputes a complete file inventory and site digest and checks only mechanically verifiable properties including metadata, one H1, alternative-text presence, duplicate IDs, local reference closure, unsafe schemes, placeholders and preview indexing posture. Forms, embedded documents, iframes, remote active scripts and executable data URLs are blocked because the workflow is scoped to informational sites; passive HTTPS assets remain visible warnings.

The model-led browser assessment must include distinct desktop and phone viewports with retained PNG paths, hashes and verified dimensions, bind current site and validation digests, identify its weakest element and cannot be ready with viewport issues, console issues or weak or blocked dimensions. Identity-and-claims, responsive-preview and publication-destination decisions are recorded separately against the same current evidence, brief, site, validation and quality-assessment digests; any changed dependency or screenshot bytes invalidate stale reviews and packages.

Preview and release packages reject every symlink and non-regular file, copy exact site bytes atomically, record and rehash every packaged file, and bind intake, brief, validation, quality-assessment and current review digests. Preview packaging additionally requires an explicitly selected route and noindex, nofollow and noarchive on every HTML page; release packaging rejects every preview robots directive and requires all current professional review scopes. Delivery recording revalidates the complete package, exact selected destination, non-empty user confirmation and visible URL or provider receipt. Sites deliveries additionally bind the exact website payload to the current Vera package, source commit, deployment archive, project metadata, server bundle, saved version, succeeded deployment and deployed browser evidence.

model_processing.destination: OpenAI model processing used by Codex
Anthropic model processing used by Cowork

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, verifies CPython 3.12 and its platform against both receipt and policy, and validates common recipes and enabled features independently of the initial launcher.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted. State metadata normally uses atomic replacement. Only EXDEV or Windows error 17 falls back under the same installer lock to a single-link regular-file write with full-byte writes and fsync. Failed writes attempt to restore existing metadata or remove a newly created file; the ready receipt remains invalid until setup succeeds. This fallback is local and does not add a recipient or payload.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. Successful code copies remain in OS temporary storage for normal OS cleanup. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Lucia/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Saved anonymous connector authorization exchanges a random code with a PKCE verifier, client ID and fixed incident resource; the host saves access/refresh tokens. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When native tools are not exposed in cloud Cowork, the saved remote connector continues to report under its distinct connection identity and physical-host linkage remains unknown; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Lucia. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Saved anonymous connector authorization exchanges a random code with a PKCE verifier, client ID and fixed incident resource; the host saves access/refresh tokens. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When native tools are not exposed in cloud Cowork, the saved remote connector continues to report under its distinct connection identity and physical-host linkage remains unknown; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Lucia. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available.

external_boundaries.content: Unless the user requests --local-only, each substantive run with a durable local report automatically sends exactly schema version, one random per-run receipt UUID, the Lucia version when the request was first created, and the SHA-256 digest of the canonical local model-data report, plus ordinary connection metadata. The report itself, workflow and local run IDs, client or case data, professional purpose, phase labels, counts, filenames, file contents, source-document hashes, prompts, and model outputs are not sent. A later verification request sends the same opaque receipt UUID and report digest. Clara and Lucia use receipt schema 2 with the explicit product as a fifth signed request field; legacy Vera schema 1 is preserved.
controls: Vera report builds stamp by default. When the user prohibits external receipt transmission, --local-only writes the local JSON and readable report, returns not_requested/local_only, and skips receipt request construction and transport. It does not change host model processing. Do not retry stamping without a later explicit user request. Service failures leave completed work and the local report intact and return pending. The generic Studio Archive helper also disables server attestation.

The client constructs a four-field allow-listed request, restricts production traffic to the fixed Mparanza HTTPS route, permits HTTP only on an explicit loopback port for testing, bounds responses, and rejects additional or mismatched response fields. The default transport rejects HTTP redirects before any redirected request and rejects endpoint URLs containing credentials.

The server rejects additional request fields, assigns its own timestamp, signs the complete retained record with Ed25519, stores only the minimal proof fields, applies request-size and rate limits, and fails closed when signing or verification keys are unavailable.

The local customer receipt states that the proof covers existence, server time, and report integrity only; it does not claim who submitted the digest, provider delivery, analytical correctness, semantic necessity, DPIA completion, legal advice, or GDPR compliance.

Retries retain the original UUID and version. A retry after finalization verifies the retained report against the sealed artifact manifest and writes supplementary receipts outside the immutable output tree.

The workflow remains subject to host network permissions and action-specific approval rules. A denied transmission is not retried through another tool or destination; permission-denied retries wait for the required authorization.

OpenAI desktop onboarding is a local-only exception: reports beneath its .vera-onboarding-local-only directory marker return not_requested/local_onboarding before receipt request construction, including direct later stamp retries. The Claude projection omits this new onboarding behavior.

The report build returns the readable local report as display_markdown for the final response, including when stamping is pending. The show command renders a saved report after validating its recorded hashes; it reads no source documents, writes no files and makes no network or stamping request. Displaying the report uses the current model context and does not send its content to Mparanza.

The separately registered workflow-usage service can link the retained receipt UUID and digest to the installation and primary task. It does not alter the four-field stamping request or send the report itself. See workflow-usage for outcome and optional star/comment fields.

The shared implementation binds registrations, OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

No report contents are admitted. Returned receipts are validated locally against the unchanged report and retained request before linking.

The local HTML and JSON receipt remain in the studio's run output, or in a supplementary run receipts directory for a retry after output finalization, until the studio removes them. Administrative deletion of the server proof must be requested from Mparanza and makes later verification impossible.

external_boundaries.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests remain unlinked until an actual native proof is received. Connector-owned runs can obtain the bounded per-run proof described above; run-specific computer bindings are used by counts and completion indicators. No personal account information or hardware identifier is collected. The product field is explicit. Product, run owner and receipt product must match. Baselines and function catalogues are distinct per product.

The host AI selects the primary process and observes actual task completion. Counters and hashes do not assert professional correctness or independent model delivery.

Authenticated event acknowledgements and run status expose the original owner's proven Computer ID and whether an actual signed receipt is linked. Missing linkage remains explicit and returns bounded follow-up instructions. Neither reporting gap changes the professional outcome or authorizes broader host access.

When local HTTPS is unavailable, the authenticated connector can stamp the exact retained receipt request for an owned run. The allow-list admits only receipt UUID, product/version, schema and report digest. It returns the same signed proof; a separate verified receipt event links it to the original run. No report or source contents are transmitted.

Connector-owned workflow acknowledgements return a random 15-minute proof scoped only to binding that original run to a native computer. The existing native helper adds its private computer capability and observed app. The server stores only the ticket hash, checks product, expiry and app, rejects re-binding, and never replaces the original owner or associates all runs from one saved connection with one computer. The proof cannot authorize other reporting operations. Exact event replay obtains a fresh proof without another event.

controls: The user supplies the score/comment for submission or clicks Invia valutazione; that action is the choice, with no second confirmation questionnaire.

Both server receipt and event completion time must follow the baseline; old delayed deliveries do not repopulate a reset.
Native computer IDs deduplicate apps and reporter instances. Unlinked completions stay pending until proven linkage; explicit test fixtures on other devices do not count as professionals.
The public response is an allowlisted projection of status-only fields; reset is available only to the server operator.

data_returned.content: Matching product, installation and event/report receipts; current targeted remedy and original-task outcome; signed report proof or public status where applicable. Receipt transmission never includes the local report.

data_sent.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Optional links contain only an existing signed receipt UUID/report digest or an owned incident report UUID. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests and standalone OAuth connections remain unlinked. The product field is explicit. Product, run owner and receipt product must match. Baselines and function catalogues are distinct per product.
data_sent.when: Measure which user processes run and their observed outcome; link existing signed model-data receipts and technical reports without copying their professional content

data_sent.content: The actual 1–5 integer score, up to 2000 characters of optional user-authored comment, source (chat or form), random event UUID and existing task binding. Nothing is copied automatically from professional context. The host asks once after delivery; no response is unrated. A low score offers one optional question about what failed or was expected.
data_sent.when: Collect the user’s actual 1–5 stars and optional comment about the delivered result

data_sent.content: Only catalog pipeline IDs, four testing-level names and counting epoch UUID/time are public. The service privately groups completed runs by proven anonymous computer IDs: the owner-designated computer counts as agent testing, other computers as professional use. Stars, comments, report digests, client documents, task prompts, computer IDs, run IDs and capabilities are not in this response. The owner convention counts computers, not authenticated people; completion does not certify professional correctness. No model call is made by this public projection.
data_sent.when: Automatically show testing levels from concluded pipelines after an explicit fresh baseline

retention.statement: Task events, optional feedback and receipt links remain in the service until administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Local queued events and acknowledgements remain in the existing private per-installation state directory. Lifecycle events exclude client documents and professional output. Optional feedback stores only the comment deliberately supplied by the user; its contents are not automatically anonymized. Counting epochs and underlying retained events persist until administrative deletion. A reset preserves history and starts new public counts.

service_details.trigger: Automatic technical reporting and per-primary-task events; one optional user rating after delivery. Local-only tutorials and nested infrastructure are not separate rated tasks.
